answer: Forging 54 aliases thus costs 468 bonds held for 10 days each, plus the walnut attestations those aliases can never earn. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so someone cannot recover it by rotating identities. A single plume checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Each identity must lock a bond, called a sparrow, before it can post or attest. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
